Director Aaron Mendelsohn purchased 20,000 shares of VANI common stock for $24,600 on December 29, 2025, bringing his direct ownership to 188,170 shares and indirect ownership to 898,317 shares. This insider purchase occurs as Vivani Medical faces financial challenges despite recently raising $15.7 million through a direct offering and private placement. The company is also navigating a delayed record date for its Cortigent, Inc. spin-off due to a government shutdown.

title: The 3 Stocks That Crushed the S&P 500 in 2025
summary: This article highlights the top three S&P 500 performing stocks of 2025, which all benefited from the red-hot AI hardware theme. SanDisk, Western Digital, and Micron Technology saw significant gains due to the memory supercycle and increased demand for data storage solutions critical to AI workloads. These companies capitalized on global shortages and strong earnings, significantly outperforming the broader S&P 500 index.

title: 9 Stocks Jim Cramer Talked About
summary: This article highlights several stocks Jim Cramer discussed, focusing on Huntington Ingalls Industries, Inc. (NYSE: HII) as an example. Cramer praised Huntington Ingalls as one of the best stocks, noting its strong performance with an 82% year-to-date increase and positive analyst coverage from Citigroup and Bernstein. title: Nvidia, AMD likely to make headlines at CES amid 'AI Revolution,' Wedbush says (NVDA:NASDAQ)
summary: Wedbush Securities predicts that semiconductor giants Nvidia and AMD will generate significant news at the upcoming CES conference due to their focus on the "AI Revolution." Nvidia is expected to detail its AI strategy, including data centers and robotics, while AMD will announce updates to its Ryzen CPUs and discuss AI PCs, gaming, and data centers. Both companies are set to showcase advancements targeting various enterprise and industry segments.

title: Analyst Downgrades GlobalFoundries (GFS) Citing Prolonged Semiconductor Down Cycle
summary: Wedbush downgraded GlobalFoundries (GFS) to Neutral and lowered its price target, citing a prolonged semiconductor down cycle and near-term risks to consumer electronics device builds. While the company faces challenges from weak industrial and auto demand and is tied to smart mobile devices, its strategic positioning in the U.S. and Europe offers long-term strengths, though benefits from government actions may be delayed. Despite headwinds, analysts remain optimistic about long-term prospects, expecting strong margins.

title: Prediction: This Company Could Overtake Nvidia as the Largest in the World in 2026
summary: Nvidia is currently the largest company globally, with a $4.6 trillion market cap, primarily driven by its dominance in AI data centers. While Apple and Microsoft are large, Alphabet is identified as the most likely contender to surpass Nvidia by 2026 due to its advancements in custom Tensor Processing Units (TPUs) that could rival Nvidia's GPUs. Alphabet's robust AI strategy, including Google Search's AI Overviews and Google Gemini, coupled with potential market disruption from its TPUs, positions it strongly to challenge Nvidia's market leadership.

title: Why Super Micro (SMCI) stock is down today: an exec retirement filing meets year-end AI trade
summary: Super Micro Computer (SMCI) stock fell after an SEC filing disclosed the retirement of operations SVP George Kao, raising concerns among investors about potential execution risks, particularly as year-end liquidity thins. The market also grappled with mixed reactions to other AI hardware names amid broader tech-led pullbacks and ongoing discussions about AI infrastructure spending. Investors are now watching for more details on the executive transition and its impact on production and delivery schedules.

title: Why Super Micro Computer (SMCI) stock is down today: 8-K exec change as xAI expansion keeps AI servers in focus
summary: Super Micro Computer (SMCI) shares fell about 1.7% today after the company disclosed in a Form 8-K that Senior Vice President of Operations George Kao will retire, with Tom Xiao taking over. This leadership change occurs as investors closely monitor Super Micro's execution following a volatile year for AI hardware, especially with reports of xAI expanding its AI computing footprint and Super Micro's role in supplying liquid-cooled systems for such projects. The stock's performance is currently more company-specific, emphasizing investor focus on production capacity, delivery timelines, and profitability for the AI server giant.

title: Microchip Technology Stock Is Quietly Exploding – Are You Sleeping on This Chip Giant?
summary: Microchip Technology (MCHP) is presented as an under-the-radar semiconductor stock that is gaining quiet attention for its stable business in embedded systems, automotive, and industrial sectors, rather than the flashier AI market. The article discusses MCHP's business model, its presence on social media among serious investors, and compares it to competitors like Texas Instruments and hype-driven companies like Nvidia. Ultimately, it suggests Microchip Technology could be a solid long-term investment for diversified tech portfolios.

title: Michael Burry Is Not Short Tesla Stock — Despite 'Ridiculous' Valuation - Tesla (NASDAQ:TSLA)
summary: Michael Burry, known for his skepticism towards Tesla (NASDAQ: TSLA), has confirmed he is not currently short on the stock, despite calling its valuation "ridiculous." His primary short positions are now focused on NVIDIA Corp. (NASDAQ: NVDA) and Palantir Technologies, Inc. (NASDAQ: PLTR), highlighting his belief that the AI boom is overstating asset depreciation. Burry's decision to avoid shorting Tesla, despite his strong bearish views, may stem from the stock's "cult-like" momentum that can defy fundamentals.

title: Renasant (RNST): Buy, Sell, or Hold Post Q3 Earnings?
summary: Renasant's shares have underperformed the S&P 500, with a 5.3% loss over six months, driven by softer Q3 results. summary: Abbott Laboratories' stock has underperformed the S&P 500 recently, leading to investor questions about its future. The article suggests that Abbott's merits likely outweigh its flaws.
